gen-gf-shantell-sans-switzer: Expressive from the first glance, Shantell Sans draws every stroke with one fixed nib and a wide-open mouth. Switzer answers with tall, wire-like letterforms that feel Swiss and approachable, plain sans polish against the hand-drawn play.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-work-sans: Work Sans brings a modern, contemporary body with a mean line set high and tips that stay well apart. Shantell Sans then adds its fixed-nib, hand-drawn character on top, a display heading that gives the pairing its personality.
gen-gf-sniglet-archivo: Round, stubby and unmistakably confident, Sniglet keeps one constant pen width from start to finish. Archivo, with its tall x-height and curves that open outward, would carry a longer passage easily.
gen-gf-sniglet-fs-asap: Sniglet draws its g in one unchanging line weight, which gives the heading a distinctive, steady beat. Asap follows with open-arc c forms and a body height nearly matching its capitals, so a long page reads smoothly.
gen-gf-sniglet-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Sniglet's terminals stop short of curling back in, and its weight never lurches anywhere along the line. Sniglet is the one to look at; Be Vietnam Pro, a plain sans, does the quiet reading.
gen-gf-sniglet-fs-epilogue: Sniglet keeps a level beat with no accents of weight. Epilogue is the looser partner, with curvy, unclamped letters, stubby ascender tips and a wire-like monoline skeleton that gives the pairing its approachable edge.
gen-gf-sniglet-fs-fira-sans: Fira Sans brings a larger-than-usual x-height and s curves that open wide at both ends, with no thick and thin contrast anywhere. Sniglet sits above it, level and commanding.
gen-gf-sniglet-fs-merriweather-sans: Sniglet has no hairlines at all, just a level, quiet beat. Shrink the heading and it holds up, while Merriweather Sans, a sans-serif with a clear-eyed e, gives sturdy, large-looking words at body size.
gen-gf-sniglet-fs-public-sans: Sniglet holds its stroke width constant, with terminals that stop short of curling back in, so headings stay distinctive and quiet. Public Sans is the hefty, trustworthy workhorse, with broad open counters.
gen-gf-sniglet-fs-ranade: Sniglet stops its terminals short of curling back in and keeps a quiet, level beat across every line. Ranade's weight shifts slightly, like stretched rubber cord, so text feels organic and spacious.
